Let  
I = ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx

Using integration by parts:

Let u = cos(x), dv = 2*exp(x) dx  
Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = 2*exp(x)

I = 2*exp(x)*cos(x) - ∫ 2*exp(x)*(-sin(x)) dx  
I = 2*exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫ 2*exp(x)*sin(x) dx

Now integrate ∫ 2*exp(x)*sin(x) dx by parts:

Let u = sin(x), dv = 2*exp(x) dx  
Then du = cos(x) dx, v = 2*exp(x)

∫ 2*exp(x)*sin(x) dx = 2*exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx  
= 2*exp(x)*sin(x) - I

Substitute back:

I = 2*exp(x)*cos(x) + 2*exp(x)*sin(x) - I  
2*I = 2*exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x))  
I = exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x)) + C

<answer>exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x)) + C</answer>
